# tomabel.ee

> Tom Kristian Abel — security researcher and systems architect. I reverse engineer how authentication and browser defenses fail, then design the systems that survive what I find.

Based in Estonia. Writes in English and Estonian. Research focuses on identity protocols (FIDO2 / WebAuthn, eIDAS, Smart-ID), anti-fraud VMs, TLS fingerprinting, and zero-trust architecture. Coordinated disclosure with RIA / CERT-EE where research touches live systems.

## Pages

- [Home](https://tomabel.ee/): Hero, featured research and systems, recent essays.
- [Disclosures](https://tomabel.ee/disclosures/): Research, teardowns, frameworks, and essays in one index (client-side filter tabs).
  - [BotGuard, disassembled — reverse engineering Google's anti-fraud VM](https://tomabel.ee/disclosures/botguard-disassembled/): an opcode-level teardown of the bytecode VM, its anti-debugging and obfuscation layers, and a token-portability weakness.
  - [The Achilles' heel of Estonia's e-state — Smart-ID / eID research](https://tomabel.ee/disclosures/smart-id-achilles-heel/): why the protocol resists MITM and endpoint attacks by design, how the approval layer fails instead, and the interactive signing-relay class of attack against Smart-ID+ cross-device QR flows. Disclosed to the vendor before publication.
  - [Zero-Trust Octagon — a framework from first principles](https://tomabel.ee/disclosures/zero-trust-octagon/): 8 axioms, a 9-dimension morphological matrix, and archetypal breach walkthroughs.
  - [PACT and the software-anchor turn — a critical analysis of Private Access Control Tokens](https://tomabel.ee/disclosures/pact-software-anchor-turn/): why Cloudflare's PACT proposal moves trust from hardware anchors to issuer judgment, and why the missing governance layer decides whether the web gets an open anti-bot layer or another trust oligopoly.
  - [The PIN that cannot be delegated — Smart-ID, AI agents, and eIDAS](https://tomabel.ee/disclosures/the-pin-that-cannot-be-delegated/): why an AI agent cannot hold your Smart-ID PIN — SK's own terms, the remote-QSCD practice statement, and eIDAS Article 26 side by side, and the OAuth-style delegation pattern that works.
  - [I used to break authentication. Here's what that taught me about building it.](https://tomabel.ee/disclosures/i-used-to-break-authentication/): the thesis essay — why understanding offense is a prerequisite for credible defense.
  - [What client-side trust is actually worth](https://tomabel.ee/disclosures/what-client-side-trust-is-actually-worth/): the BotGuard teardown as a case study for why any defense running on a machine you don't control is a claim, not a proof — and what to build instead.
  - [The kratt problem](https://tomabel.ee/disclosures/the-kratt-problem/): offensive capability as Estonian folklore — a servant that works tirelessly while pointed and turns on its maker when idle; ethics as a pointing problem.
  - [Coordinated disclosure in a small country](https://tomabel.ee/disclosures/coordinated-disclosure-in-a-small-country/): what national-infrastructure disclosure looks like in Estonia, where everyone knows each other — the legal exposure, the incentives, and why owning your story in public is the protection that scales.
  - [The fix that doesn't need SK](https://tomabel.ee/disclosures/the-fix-that-doesnt-need-sk/): the Achilles' heel report's five fixes all need SK, a bank, or a regulator to move — a sixth, session-continuity checking at a bank's own edge, doesn't, scoped honestly to the cross-device relay case.
  - [ChatGPT is not a phishing scanner](https://tomabel.ee/disclosures/chatgpt-is-not-a-phishing-scanner/): a fact check of the "paste the suspicious link into ChatGPT" advice — what ChatGPT, Claude, and Gemini actually document, why TDS cloaking can feed a single AI fetch a decoy page, and why VirusTotal and Safe Browsing remain the verdict layer.
  - [The evolution of cyber fraud in Estonia, 2010–2026](https://tomabel.ee/disclosures/the-evolution-of-cyber-fraud-in-estonia/): how Estonia's small language held the fraud industry at arm's length for a decade, and what happened when the barrier fell — recruited native speakers, industrialized vishing call centers, courier networks, and AI deepfakes, with annual losses climbing to €29 million in 2025.
  - [The Gray Space: Russian Cyber Operations and Estonian Hosting Infrastructure](https://tomabel.ee/disclosures/russian-cyber-ops-estonia-hosting/): an OSINT assessment of Estonia's dual role in the Russian cyber ecosystem — mainstream providers, bulletproof hosts like Vault Dweller OÜ, and gray-space proxy networks (Fineproxy, Quality Network OÜ) anchored in Estonian data centers.
  - [How client-side anti-fraud actually works, and why VLMs break it](https://tomabel.ee/disclosures/why-vlms-break-client-side-anti-fraud/): how client-side anti-fraud actually works, why the old arms race was about forgery, and why a vision-language model driving a real browser sidesteps it entirely — plus which of the five paradigms survive and the attestation centralization problem.
  - [The Nine Dimensions of Zero Trust](https://tomabel.ee/disclosures/nine-dimensions-of-zero-trust/): the nine-dimension morphological matrix laid out axis by axis — what each dimension decides, the realistic range of positions, and why "are we zero trust?" is the wrong question.
  - [The Fortune 500 Illusion of Control](https://tomabel.ee/disclosures/the-fortune-500-illusion-of-control/): a step-by-step breach trace of Archetype B — the enterprise with the largest budget and the most attestations — from stolen session cookie to full database export in twenty minutes. Analytical composite, not a real incident.
  - [Move Fast, Fix It In Prod: A Full Breach Trace of the Startup Archetype](https://tomabel.ee/disclosures/move-fast-fix-it-in-prod/): the full supply-chain and CI/CD trace for Archetype C: dependency to pipeline to credential to production, and why the automation that makes a startup fast is what makes the blast radius large.
  - [SaaS-Glued Lean Defense: The Full Breach Trace for Archetype D](https://tomabel.ee/disclosures/saas-glued-lean-defense/): the breach trace for the most common architecture of all — one operator, a dozen SaaS products: MFA fatigue, the OAuth grant cascade, and five fixes that need an afternoon rather than a budget.
  - [Identity Is the Root. Proof Is the Gate.](https://tomabel.ee/disclosures/identity-is-the-root-proof-is-the-gate/): the capstone argument connecting the zero-trust work to the eID research: every control is downstream of identity, a login is a point-in-time assertion, and the approval layer is where real systems fail.
- [Systems](https://tomabel.ee/systems/): Shipped systems — fingerprintproxy (production Go TLS-fingerprinting proxy, 65+ browser profiles, JA3/JA4), Vooglaadija (FastAPI media-extraction service with Redis queues, JWT auth, observability), Discord RAG pipeline (LanceDB + BM25 hybrid retrieval with RBAC-aware filtering).
- [About](https://tomabel.ee/about/): Bio, philosophy, and the kratt metaphor.
- [My story](https://tomabel.ee/my-story/): How I got here, in three acts — the criminal case, the pivot from offense to research, and the published work as evidence. Links the original Delfi interview.
- [Privacy Policy](https://tomabel.ee/privacy/), [Terms of Service](https://tomabel.ee/terms/), [Cookie Policy](https://tomabel.ee/cookies/), [Security Research Policy](https://tomabel.ee/disclosure/)
